and the modeling of the changeability of the surrounding world. Under the
"dictate" of the algorithm of the principle of self-development the correlation
of the components-constituents in the known relation {change/basis}
constantly changes, as a result of which at every moment there is realized
the "changing basis", reproducing itself thanks to ever new and new
contentful layers, — which is why it does not become exhausted, which is
why the very development of reality does not cease.
At every moment the "lived-through" becomes the "building material" for the
"coming" present, "winding" and layering onto the still more distant past (the
"lived-through"). Only such a way of movement-development as "the making
of oneself from oneself", such a course of events, similar to "winding",
insures and delivers the future from the detailed repetitions of the past. By
the simple "copying" or "reflection" no single process is realized in full
measure; the contrary — is from the category of delusions and chimeras. In
reality there takes place the permanent movement in the direction of novelty
and unrepeatability on the basis of the uniqueness of everything
"accomplishing itself". The very character, type, and way of the movementself-development excludes the repeatability and reversibility of the forms.
The appearance of new content in new forms cannot be explained in any way
by the "copying" or "reflection" of the external world by the organs of sense
(sensations) and by the thinking of the cognizing subject [11, p. 125, 151].
The new content arises and is realized in new forms because it "winds" one
layer onto another with the accompanying changes of all the layers (by virtue
of the absorption by the layers of these changes) and, correspondingly, with

 the differences of the content of the subsequent forms from the content of
the preceding ones.
Man, animal, plant breathes, drinks, eats, interacts with the external world,
and precisely in such a way — by the path of the layering of changes onto
the basis — there is carried out the feeding, replenishment, renewal of the
developing content of the living forms (including the subjectively ideal forms
of human thinking). On the simplest things, on the ordinary and everyday
examples one can be convinced of this again and again. In particular, the
organism in the state of sleep is precisely that basis, that foundation onto
which the changes and new volumes of content accumulated by the organism
in the period of its activity are "mounted", into which they are built in. On the
example of sleep it is well noticeable that the layers are attached to the basis
not evenly and uninterruptedly, but by diverse portions, alternating with
pauses, rest, "repose", etc.
In what is seen the "sense" of the life or existence of the plant, animal, man?
In that, by the different levels of their multilevel formations, to assimilate,
express, comprehend the contentful accumulations in the calculation (with
anticipation) of the subsequent assimilation, expression, and comprehension
of new, still greater volumes of diverse contentful accumulations.
Copying and photographing does not give true representations of the current
processes in the multilevel reality (including at the level of self-cognition). As
reflection or copying this can be perceived and carried out only in immobility,
in statics, in the form of a particular case of the universal movement; in
dynamics, in development — this is always "winding", "making from
oneself"... The development-movement-change of actuality is the generation
and embodiment of the objectively realizing principle of self-development
(initially present in any "something", in any element of reality), which gives
the representation and testifies about the intensifying movement of the
content (of reality) onto the coverage and comprehension of the very same
moving content in its ever more and more "embryonic" state. In the same
way there is carried out also the process of cognition as the movement of the
specific (gnoseological) form of reality at the level and in the terms of human
thinking.
As for the question of the cognizability of the surrounding world, then in the
final account it will inevitably be necessary to come to the understanding of
the circumstance that the world — this is not a book and all the more not a
rock or a boulder-stone in its immutability, but something unceasingly
"making itself", reproducing itself, changing itself in the regime of real time;
and a similar question in a correct formulation must be posed not in relation
to the cognizability of something given and existing from the age in its
constancy, but in relation to the possibility of the foresight and anticipation of
the newly arising forms (including the consequences, results, events,
configurations, situations) of the developing reality.

 The levels of development are often inseparable, undetachable from each
other for the reason that the contentful constituent, say, of one level can at
one and the same time (in interconnection) turn out to be the formal
constituent for another level and vice versa. And also for the reason that the
contentful constituent of one level necessarily represents a new relation
{content/form} for another level. The same thing should be said also about
any formal constituent. But the main obstacle on the path of the clear
understanding of the course of the process of development and of its exact
formulations consists in the fact that the natural boundary between the
components-constituents "content" and "form" in their relation is hardly
distinguishable, and at times simply not perceptible (for the time being).
Thus, the ingrowing of the levels-forms into each other and their growing out
of one another is precisely the cause of the impossibility of their separation in
a "pure" form, as well as of the intricacy of the processes and of the difficulty
of the expression (explanation) of the unexplored, and in some sense
irrational, through the comprehended rational.
In such a connection one must always take into account the dual nature of
the world, and especially in the cases when the matter concerns the
examination and investigation of intricate (and precisely therefore complex)
questions. This thought is far from new, we simply often forget about it. And
in order to come out onto the correct solution of the fundamental problems,
without the dialectical approach it is already in no way possible to get by.
The striving to express the new abstract content through the preceding more
concrete forms by virtue of the effect of the winding of content, described
and conditioned (the speech is about the effect of winding) by the
formulation of the principle of self-development, leads to the search of a new
form for the new content, which is the continuation of all the other contentful
forms present in the linkage or in the aggregate. This form includes in itself
in the "sublated", concentrated form the preceding manifestations of the
essence of the object and simultaneously is their continuation, expansion,
and superstructure with the "inclusions" of some peculiarities (differences)
not present until then in the preceding forms. Therefore the main thing that
one should catch in this process is not the "reflection" of one in the other
(not the doubling or multiplication of essences), but the transformation, the
transformation of the available linkage of the preceding forms into a new
aggregate form, and moreover not equivalent to the simple sum of the
forms, but qualitatively different from it.
The life and existence of man as the subject of cognition — this is the
movement of the contentful constituent through the forms-levels in the
direction of the acquisition of the most contentful form of such a movement,
which is precisely what is affirmed by the formulation of the principle of selfdevelopment. In words we, as the embodiment of the predominantly
conservative component-constituent of the relation {change/basis}, i.e., of
the "basis", of course, can deny that at every moment by each our action, by
each breath in and out, by each word and deed (being simultaneously the

 personification also of the second component-constituent of the relation, i.e.,
of the "change") we participate in the search and creation of the most
contentful forms of our existence and development; however, in fact
everything indicates that there is no alternative to this process.
§ 16. The systematization and refinement of some notions and
definitions in the light of our representations about the development
and cognition of reality
Let us attempt to systematize what has been set forth above, breaking
through, as before, through the veil of delusions and confusion in the notions
and representations about the subject of our conversation.
The truthfulness of a form is determined by its contentfulness; hence the
criterion of truth or of the truthfulness of the forms is served by their
contentfulness. The more contentful the form, the more truthful it is. The
internal contentfulness of a form reveals itself by diverse external
manifestations, executions, embodiments.
From time immemorial man observes and fixes the multitude of
manifestations of the internal contentfulness of the forms, such as: beauty
and elegance, simplicity, harmony, laconism, systemicity, economy, noncontradictoriness, self-sufficiency, etc. For the establishment and
confirmation of the truthfulness of any form all these manifestationsexecutions of its contentfulness must pass one and the same procedure of
assessment — interpretation, — consisting in the determination of the
possibility and admissibility of the substitution of the contents of the
investigated forms by the contents of as large as possible a number of
concrete and abstract forms, the truthfulness of which has already been
confirmed and does not raise doubts.
The matter remains only for the fact that with respect to each concrete
manifestation or execution of contentfulness one should find (reveal, select)
its own specific standards for the correct determination of the "quantity" of
this contentfulness and the expression of it in conventional units. The more
such manifestations falling into the field of vision of the human
consciousness, the more complex, all-embracing, and informative the
criterion of the assessment of the truthfulness of the forms turns out to be;
in other words, if all the manifestations of contentfulness are gathered
together, then there will be obtained the combined criterion of the all-round
assessment of the truthfulness of any form, — by the aggregate of the
manifestations of the contentfulness of this form.
Hence, apparently, proceeds also the intuitive striving of a number of
researchers to introduce a certain complex criterion of the assessment of
truth; the striving itself is quite natural and justified, all the more so that in
many fields of human activity, conditioned and generated by the different
manifestations of the contentfulness of all possible forms, the criteria of the

 assessment of the truthfulness of the forms have already been worked out
and exist, in others — they are still to be worked out. But with all the
perspectiveness of the indicated idea one should nevertheless stop on the
peculiarities of its interpretation and embodiment.
"We suppose, — write the authors, — that the synthesis of the existing
conceptions of truth is possible. The core of the general theory of truth can
become the conception of correspondence, in connection with the fact that
only it discloses the essence of true knowledge. According to the words of
Descartes, who clearly and most briefly formulated the main idea of the
theory of correspondence, "truth... means the correspondence of the thought
to the object". ... Without the correlation with the object the notion of truth
has no sense, there is no objectless truth, no truth about nothing" [4, p. 6—
7].
On the example of the cited quotation let us examine the confusion in the
representations, about which we have declared above. The matter is that in
this fragment of the article (as also in the multitude of publications on this
theme) there is compared the not quite comparable, similar, say, to the
attempt of the establishment of the correspondence between meters and
seconds. Despite the fact that both the one and the other "grow" from one
root as the components-constituents of the integral relation {time/space},
nevertheless they are not equivalent and not identical to each other, just as
the components of the primordial relation {content/form} are not identical
and not interchangeable. Here there is evident the attempt to correlate and
identify the "formal" and "contentful" beginnings of reality, which by and
large is incorrect by virtue of their natural incompatibility.
The truthfulness of knowledge is determined by its contentfulness. The fuller,
the higher the contentfulness of knowledge, the more truthful, more reliable
it is. As we see, the objectness here is generally beside the point.
The necessity of the "correlation with the object" appears not in connection
with the assessment of the truthfulness of knowledge, but in connection with
the assessment of the fullness or the "quantity" of its contentfulness, which
(the assessment) is carried out, as has been said above, by means of the
procedure of practice or the technology of interpretation, i.e., by the
comparison and substitution (as complete as possible) of the content of the
abstract form of knowledge by the contents of the more concrete forms of
sensations and/or by the contents of the abstract forms of thinking, the
truthfulness of which has already been confirmed and does not raise doubts.
And only on the basis of the established contentfulness of knowledge can
one speak about its truthfulness. The truthfulness of this or that form, thus,
has no direct relation to objectness (if only for the reason that the
confirmations of truthfulness are equally required by both the abstract and
the empirical forms or the forms of sensations, closely connected with the
thing forms). The truthfulness of the abstract forms is correlated with
objectness only indirectly — through the procedure of the assessment and
establishment of the fullness of the contentfulness of the abstract forms.

 For this same reason the verbal turns of speech of the type "the
correspondence of the thought to the object" (in the formulation of
Descartes) or "the correlation of the notion with the object" (in the modern
formulation) from ancient times and up to this day are used incorrectly with
respect to the procedure of the search of truth or the establishment of the
truthfulness of knowledge. One should not forget that the subjective human
knowledge about a real object serves as the expression of the objective
content of the form of the object, already mediated by the form of human
sensations and by the form of human thinking. Therefore only the contents of
the form of sensations and of the form of thinking can be compared,
correlated, tested for correspondence. And only on the basis of the revealed
(in the process of comparison and correlation) to some extent conjugacy,
correspondence, equivalence, or "coincidence" of these contents, only then
can one make the conclusion about some commonality and continuity of their
forms, and, consequently, about the objectivity of the contents of the forms
of sensations and thinking, supplementing, deepening, and developing the
objective content of the form of the object itself. By virtue of the
indicated circumstance the objective content of the form of the object
appears already in the quality of the objective content of the generalized
multilevel aggregate (symbiosis) of all the three conjugated successive
forms of the different levels (the form of thingness, the form of sensations,
and the form of thinking). Finally, the content of the above-mentioned
aggregate of forms, manifested by means of the form of thinking, with the
objectivity certified (with the help of the procedure of practice or the
technology of interpretation) (i.e., with the highest contentfulness) can lay
claim to the status of true knowledge about the object.
Thus, the content of the abstract form (of knowledge, thought, etc.) requires
the "correlation" or "correspondence" not with the object (objectness, being,
etc.), but with the content of the thing form, and moreover mediated by the
form of sensations. And already on the basis of the mentioned correlation

development). The changes that become isolated and "tear away" from the
basis liquidate the relation as a whole as such, since something, being
deprived of the basis and "not remembering kinship", is transformed into its
opposite. The vector of development is to a considerable degree determined
by the basis, i.e., by the past, by the "lived-through", by the preceding
accumulations.
The role of Russia as the main stabilizing component or counterbalance in the
system {West/East}, threatening at times to go to pieces, — is indisputable.
True, the most effectively this counterbalance will function only on the basis
of the renewed social structure with the socialist order, which, undoubtedly,
is our national priority and pride for centuries.
The absence (especially among politicians) of adherence to such, for
example, qualities of man and indicators of the developed harmonious
society as honor, conscience, decency, morality, ethics, philanthropy, mutual
respect — is a direct path "into non-being" for those human communities
which refuse such humanistic acquisitions, ideals, and convictions.
The inadequate behavior of the majority of individuals (of society), as a
reaction to the movement into nowhere, "sanctified" by contentless goals, is
punished by "non-being", i.e., by the absorption and assimilation of the lowcontentful forms by the healthy adequate forms. Russia, with its considerably
more adequate than that of the collective West representations about reality,
has every chance for leadership with a humanistic orientation, provided that
a way is found to transform the ugly and defective capitalist forms imposed
on it into other harmonious forms of development.
As time and the course of the developing events show, the subjective, it
would seem, question of the justice of the social structure [Roman law, for
example, refers the notion of justice to the subjective categories] turns out
to be a question not at all subjective, but exclusively objective. Taking into
account the striving and craving for justice originally inherent in our people,
the following ideological scheme or chain of contentful transformations has
quite matured for embodiment at a new level: truth (verity) => justice
=>law =>equality => (social) equilibrium =>balance =>harmony ... Any
human community or civilization in one way or another (explicitly and
implicitly) strives for the realization of such a chain, conditioned by the
dialectical nature of the surrounding world. In reality — this is a
question of life and death for all the human communities presently existing.
It is worth, perhaps, to dwell separately on the role and significance of
modern advertising.

 Today's aggressive advertising on TV — this is, as a rule, well-paid lie and
deliberately distorted representation of the true state of affairs. In the
language of advertising, from the tenderest nails, a signal is sent to man:
one can lie a lot and with impunity, from a high tribune and to a multi-million
audience. Advertising almost always peremptorily hypertrophies the limited
positive and advantage of the goods, services, and all sorts of "brands",
hiding in the backyard their negative features and shortcomings. In this
consists its lie, by this it perniciously influences the unformed young minds.
The lying advertising from morning till evening teaches the youth also to
treat easily and undemandingly their own unfulfilled promises and empty
assurances.
Advertising must be removed from TV unambiguously. The most "creative"
liars cry out that without advertising there will be no TV. They lie,
shamelessly lie, for the principles of the functioning of TV are deliberately
distorted and disfigured by the dealers from TV. Those lie who have a
relation to the huge money that revolves in this backstage and that can be
uncontrollably stuffed into pockets. In the conditions of the social character
of production and the private-capitalist mode of appropriation, the throwing
of dust in the eyes of the respectable public — is an inalienable element of all
television shows and attractions. When the matter concerns the distribution
and appropriation of the product worked out under capitalism, everyone
must immediately forget about the transparency of these procedures —
otherwise by no forces will it be possible to gather on relatively tiny patches
the transcendent number of crooks and other odious individuals.
Meanwhile, the way around these "naturally" organized difficulties is quite
well-known and artless — to create an accumulation fund, public
consumption funds and to feed with them the vital and demanded directions,
and not only on TV; this is, perhaps, so far the most effective and tested way
of the development of human initiatives in the conditions of the coming
socialist order.
Let us touch upon the background of the origin and rooting of false premises.
A lie — this is also a certain contentful form, but with an extremely low
degree of objective contentfulness, i.e., a form of a very distant (rough)
approximation to the expression of the objective content of reality (a lowcontentful, and therefore untruthful form).
A shameless lie — this is a factual refusal of the moral-ethical norms and
categories in favor of a temporary, momentary, as a rule, material gain (with
its single measure — the volume of the money supply). To such a choice is
brought by the cultivation of the vividly expressed individualism in opposition
to collectivism and the priority of public interests.
The inability and unwillingness to distinguish the inessential or little-essential
from the essential, firstly, and the arbitrary absolutization of this little-

 essential to the detriment of the essential, secondly, — is akin to an
impudent shameless lie. Using such a device one can for a long time
effectively make mountains out of molehills, deliberately belittling the
contentfulness of the essential forms. The conscious belittling of the essential
and the exaltation of the inessential is equivalent to the mixing of lie with
half-truth, and therefore this is the most refined, vile, and disgusting variety
of lie. However, sooner or later the natural installation on the growth of the
contentfulness of the forms will take its toll and will arrange the forms in
their places according to the level of their contentfulness.
Every lie — this is a deliberate attempt to lead aside and to evade the
adequate thinking.
When we are tried to be convinced that black is white, referring to the
truthfulness of the generally valid (i.e., to the opinion of a certain "little
collective" that has gathered under its banners a limited number of
individuals), then these propagandists of the generally valid to the detriment
of the objective must bear in mind that the answer for the imposition of a
failed opinion may, as it may turn out, have to be held not before the
hoodwinked "little collective", but before the deceived humanity.
Virtual reality — this is a lie based on the unsupported and unconfirmed by
the content of concrete forms admissibility of the prevalence of the
subjective constituent in the relation {subjective/objective} to the detriment
of the objective constituent. The modern cinematography of the "overseas"
Hollywood type (which has splendidly mastered the "Solzhenitsyn" motives
and devices of inflating the less essential to scales surpassing everything
essential) is saturated with fictions, tricks, and special effects, hindering the
adequate perception of reality. The indulgence of the "overseas" inadequacy
again is fraught with consequences for the whole world.
In the final account, this is the right of every individual to choose — in which
direction and to what extent one should shift the dividing line in the relation
{subjective/objective}, but, fortunately, the criterion of the correctness and
admissibility of such "shifts" nevertheless exists; this is the adequacy of the
content of thinking to the content of being. In the case of the absolutization
of the component "subjective", the harmless, at first glance, inadequacy of
thinking and of the formed representations about reality can lead to serious
consequences. The above-mentioned "little collective" or a certain limited
community and its collective consciousness is capable of existing in the
"fake" regime of the inadequate perception of reality only for a very limited
time as well, but even in a short period it can create a global threat to the
survival of humanity as a whole, and even destroy it ...
Let us cite a somewhat hyperbolized and therefore quite obvious for
comprehension example. Suppose, from the apartment of the seventh floor
there are two exits outside: through the door and through the window.
Everyone knows that one can go out both through the door and through the

 window, but the overwhelming majority habitually uses the door, since it
knows that the exit through the window is fraught with grave consequences.
And nevertheless there are separate individuals who, following obsessive
ideas, leave the apartment through the window, and for one reason or
another their number will never be reduced to zero. The realization of such
an alternative possibility on the scale of the whole humanity would threaten
the disappearance of humanity as a species. The loss of the adequacy of the
representations about reality in this case could turn out to be critical and be
expressed in the loss of humanity as a definite level of reality. The speech
here is precisely about such a "can" which "cannot" from the point of view of
the adequately thinking man (and of humanity as a whole). [Deliberately
exaggerated examples sometimes help to feel the real danger of flirting with
inadequacy].
Another example. The Ptolemaic picture of the world proceeded from the
primacy of the geocentric representations. Was this inadequacy of
representations critical for those times? Probably, no. But with time, little by
little, it became such. In any case, no accuracy of the calculation of the
trajectory of the flight of space vehicles on the basis of the Ptolemaic model
(because of the transcendent cumbersomeness and error of the calculations)
could be out of the question today.
Thinking easily shifts the boundary in the relation {subjective/objective} in
the direction of the prevalence of the subjective (for itself, as for the most
abstracted level of reality, this is not critical), but at the same time it can, to
the detriment of adequacy, provoke the "exit" of the values of the whole
relation beyond the limits of the range admissible by this definite stage of
development. In other words, for "proper" thinking some inadequate
preferences and unbridled internal activity (while they are localized in the
head, without exit outside) can remain and without consequences, but for
the whole linkage-aggregate of the levels of man (dwelling in the thing world
and including in itself the form of thingness, the form of sensations, and the
form of thinking) — the arbitrary choice of thinking with the subsequent exit
of the inadequate reactions outside can turn out to be critical, which is shown
by the examples cited above.
A lie is often dictated by the striving to adapt to the external conditions and
influences in the name of the survival and prosperity of some separate formlevel in isolation from the remaining levels of the general aggregate in the
composition of the structure of man (say, the exaltation of the flesh and
material acquisitions to the detriment or bypass of morality and ethics). At
the same time, at the mental level there "reigns" a factual "dual power"
(split): something more formal collides with something more contentful. As a
result, a conflict arises: the contentful constituent "supervises", as a rule,
directly the straightforward, artless path of the achievement of the goal; the
formal constituent, however, for the sake of the achievement of the goal, as
it seems, by a more sure-fire path, is ready to go roundabout, i.e., to lie.

 Truth and lie — forms of deliberately different degrees of approximation to
the expression of the fullness of the moving (objective) content. By virtue of
the perniciousness of the influence of even the smallest public "fakes" and
fictions on the minds and consciousness of people, one must fight against lie
harshly, resolutely, and mercilessly — to suppress, not leaving without
attention a single serious attempt of the rooting of falsity. When the question
arises about the survival of humanity or of its separate communities, the
orientation to the inadequate thinking, false premises, and "values" not
approved by life is categorically inadmissible.
In order not to find oneself on the sidelines of development, the
contentfulness of all without exception forms (ideas, perspective plans,
projects, programs, directions, etc.) planned on the state scale for
development and embodiment must be analyzed and ranked at the state and
public levels in a permanent and uninterrupted regime.
However, not only mean, petty, or mercenary motives and goals are the
background of the fake injections and the spread of lies. Their "feasible"
contribution of confusion to the public life is made by the humanitarians,
who, by virtue of their professional orientation to the world of people and the
sphere of psychology, live in isolation from the physical world and are easily
intoxicated by the ruling "top", poorly imagining how bread grows, steel is
boiled, and energy is released at the fission of the uranium nucleus. The
widening illiteracy in the questions of natural science — also one of the
causes of the false representations about the world, of the spread and
tenacity of myths.
The unprincipledness of the position and the absence of firm convictions
among the statesmen and ordinary citizens in a similar way is akin to the
renunciation of truth and the patronage of lie.
The "comprador guts" of the powers that be and of the so-called business —
again from the same series.
The very widespread opinion on that score that the market allegedly will put
everything in its places, both in the sphere of production and consumption,
— also a lie or at least a dense delusion. If already by chance, unexpectedly
(well, they overlooked, "missed", with whom it does not happen!) there
arose man with his thinking (and, correspondingly, everything connected
with him, the so-called "artificial"), then, most likely, he in one way or
another consciously and unconsciously will interfere and in the nature of all
things (or this is already generally beyond the limits of understanding?).
Getting burned and making mistakes and learning on them, man will
constantly correct both his own life and the influence of the external
environment — another path of development, except for the "making of
oneself from oneself", simply does not exist. For this reason both the state
planning, and the state support, and the state regulation in various fields of
production and consumption are quite regular and will certainly be present as

 a consequence of the vision of the processes of development by the eyes of
the subject (the initiator of everything "artificial"). Another matter is that
with all this the question remains as before topical, which also no one is able
to cancel and which the subjective consciousness will have to solve
permanently in the name of the provision of the steady contentful
development — the finding of the optimal correlation or balance of the
mutually complementary components of the "invisible hand of the market"
and the "state regulation" (i.e., the balance or optimal correlation of the
artificial and the natural).
And, finally, one cannot fail to see today how destructive a weapon (a
weapon of mass destruction) the information pandemic can turn out to be
and how important it is to be able to verify and establish the truthfulness of
the information injections. In such a connection, the significance and role of
the technology of interpretation (in solving the problem of the establishment
of truth) as a means of counteracting the threat of the infliction on humanity
of all kinds of damage of a global scale by means of cunningly planned
information attacks increase immeasurably.
Unfortunately, we do not have the possibility to develop this theme further
here.
Everywhere, at all levels of the development of reality, between all its forms
of all levels without exception there takes place a harsh competitive struggle
for the possession of the highest contentfulness or the struggle for the
contentful resource, which turns out to be a direct consequence of the
universality of the principle of self-development. The striving to the
expression of truth and verity, determined by this same principle, is originally
inherent, including, in the very "mechanism" of human thinking
(consciousness). And if today a certain lie is considered an ordinary and
habitual matter and is accepted "with a bang" by undemanding collectives
and communities, then tomorrow there will certainly be found a subject (or
subjects) who, obeying the immanent principle of self-development present
in him, will "dig up" the truth about this falsity, and all the constructions
erected on lying premises will collapse in an instant, and even with the
attendant consequences for those who erected the lie on a pedestal.
Moreover, such a scenario is realized by no means by reason of the
intervention of "higher forces", but under the "pressure" of the objectively
everywhere present universal, unconditional, blind, and relative principle of
self-development with its "installations" on the possession of the maximally
achievable contentfulness by all forms-levels of the changing reality.
Conclusions
The above set forth we consider a sufficient basis for the following
conclusions.
1. The objective reality represents the movement and change of its forms in
the direction of the possession by the mentioned forms of the highest

 contentfulness. The cognitive process can be more effective if the
development of reality is examined from the position of the content-form
transformations of unitary directionality.
2. The human consciousness (thinking) — this is the most abstracted (of the
reliably known today) form of the representation of the content of reality,
continuing by itself the series of the preceding forms, such as the form of
thingness and the form of sensations. Getting rid of the representations
about consciousness as an "reflection" or "copy" of reality, human thinking
acquires the possibility to see the development of reality as a single
("through") movement of its content by means of ever more abstracting
contentful forms; thereby the artificial gnoseological barrier is eliminated,
erected by the human consciousness itself on the path of the cognition of the
contentfully infinite (multilevel) movement of reality.
3. The genuine criterion of truth or of the truthfulness of the forms of
the developing reality is established. The truthfulness of this or that
form of reality is determined by the fullness or the "quantity" of its
contentfulness. Hence, the criterion of the truthfulness of the forms
of reality is served by their contentfulness.
4. The above-mentioned criterion makes it possible to quantitatively assess
the contentfulness of the forms of reality, which gives the possibility to
arrange them by rank and thereby more precisely and more meaningfully
determine the direction of the perspective investigations.
5. Practice is not the criterion of truth, but serves as a procedure
(technology, way) of the assessment of the fullness or the "quantity" of the
contentfulness of all sorts of forms of reality. In the indicated sense practice
represents a particular case of the more general technology, named
interpretation.
6. The essence of the process of cognition is reduced to the fact that
everything investigated and uncognized is assessed, verified, and expressed
through the available and existing, the truthfulness of which has already
been established and verified by time.
7. There do not exist two or more equally contentful truths (ideas,
representations, assertions, theories, conceptions, models, opinions, points
of view, etc.) with respect to one and the same investigated question or
subject of judgment, just as there cannot be in principle two or more
equivalent approximations to the objective truth or to the absolute truth. At
any given moment of development among the forms of different
approximations there exists only one form, the most approximated to the
form of the objective (absolute) contentfulness. This is precisely the form on
which one should orient oneself as on the true one.

title: Article 4. Unlearned Lessons of Dialectics: From Whom and How to Learn to Think

text:
ARTICLE 4
Unlearned Lessons of Dialectics: From Whom and How to Learn to Think
Dialectically
Abstract
This article is dedicated to the lessons of dialectics from Vladimir I. Lenin — an
outstanding national thinker to whom the ability of clear dialectical thinking was
generously gifted by nature. Any work that came from Lenin's pen is imbued
with the spirit of dialectics.
Any Lenin's thought is a chain or series of conceptual forms maximally filled with
objective content. Any of his theoretical work is a model of masterfully balanced
sliding of thought as if on the "razor's edge", the opposite sides-facets of which
symbolize the confrontation of two non-identical opposing sides-components of
reality.
The aim of this article is to draw the attention primarily of the young reader
precisely to these qualities of Vladimir I. Lenin's theoretical works.
In the course of familiarizing oneself with Lenin's theoretical heritage, the
circumstance that the research approach he used remains unclaimed to this day,
and Lenin's lessons of dialectics, accordingly, remain unlearned, catches the eye.
Since at the foundation of any certain form of reality (object, process,
phenomenon) lie two highly abstract and non-identical, yet at the same time
objective and interrelated constituent sides-components "content" and "form",
the content-form relations (conversions, transformations) come to the fore and
become the subject of close attention of dialectics.
Considering Lenin's theoretical works through the prism of content-form relations
and identifying on this basis the general regularities of the construction and
presentation of material makes it possible to speak about the possibility of
creating a single universal methodology for conducting effective research at any
level and in any field of reality.
Introduction

 As an epigraph to this article, we would like to take words by Vladimir I. Lenin
from his work "On the Road", written in 1909: "...this stage must be outgrown;
the new circumstances of the moment require new forms of struggle..." [8, p.
540].
The cited quote, in our view, vividly expresses not only the character of a
remarkable living and flexible personality but also the essence of the entire life
and revolutionary activity of V.I. Lenin: keenly and relentlessly tracking the
situation, accurately grasping its changes, and being constantly ready to respond
to these changes with the most adequate actions — new forms of struggle.
In this article, we will examine and analyze the greatness and scale of Lenin's
figure from the standpoint of his innate ability: to be a dialectician. Discarding
all fictional, doubtful and secondary elements that were thrust into the
foreground during the "murky" 1990s — years of merciless reprisals against
Soviet power and the USSR — we will focus mainly on this aspect of Lenin's
activities and personality in our research.
A dialectical mindset is that indispensable trait of Lenin's individuality which, in
our opinion, has not yet received due coverage in fiction and journalism. All
other attributes of genius are already derivatives of such outstanding features of
his nature: adherence to a scientific approach in studying any issues; striving for
objective and impartial presentation of conclusions and results obtained through
observations and studies, etc. It was precisely Lenin's natural "immersion" in the
mysterious medium of dialectics that provoked fierce hostility and rejection
towards him from his enemies and opponents who, lacking this natural gift,
could boast of nothing more than inventing plots "out of their heads" and
presenting scholastic twists, assumptions, fables and fairy tales.
Another reason for pathological hatred and animosity toward Lenin's personality
lies in the inability of his opponents to achieve a penetrating, Lenin-like insight
into the essence and order of things; and this unattainable depth of
understanding actual relations remains the main irritant for his opponents even
now.
What is the strength of Lenin, if even his most die-hard detractors and
adversaries nevertheless recognize his influence and authority on a global scale?
First of all, in our view, it lies in his philosophical significance and specifically in
mastery of dialectics: when foresight is the result of a talent of an individual to
see the development of reality through the prism of interaction between directly
opposing sides of this (reality). He was what many ordinary and extraordinary
philosophizing individuals secretly desire and dream of becoming, realizing
however that they fall short, do not measure up, and cannot become anyone
similar — because some extremely important constituent elements are missing
in the multi-layered structure of their own "I".
It is difficult to find a modern public leader who stands at least level with (on the
same step) Lenin — an encyclopedic scholar and philosopher of profound depth,

 a brilliant polemicist, consistent and fearless revolutionary, prominent politician
and outstanding statesman.
Possession of the invaluable gift of a born dialectician allowed Lenin to handle
events and circumstances with exquisite precision, balancing on the crest of the
wave.
The accuracy and precision with which historical figures of a dialectical "leaven"
walk along the "razor's edge", balancing between Scylla and Charybdis in
interpreting the questions under study, evokes admiration and envy in the best
sense of the word. Through them (and via them), dialectics charts its way most
effectively and optimally. It is precisely through them and their voices that
dialectically developing nature speaks to us.
It is regrettable, of course, that the beauty and perfection of thought, say, of
Marx or Engels can be appreciated by most of us only thanks to the efforts of
translators. Undoubtedly, those translators of the time were highly qualified
specialists and quite exceptional people, but as someone aptly noted, reading
classics in translation is like taking a shower while wearing a coat. And so much
the better that the beauty, clarity and precision of Lenin's thought can, thank
god, be known and evaluated without the interference of intermediary
translators.
All people (especially outstanding ones) are to one degree or another
spontaneous dialecticians. And it does not matter what craft (of mental or
physical labor) they possess. Dialectics, ingrained in the flesh and blood of every
person, occasionally orients him/her towards certain paradoxical (it seems, from
the point of view of common sense) solutions, thanks to which he/she achieves
remarkable results and therefore becomes famous among the general public. We
refer here, for example, to memoirs and recollections of celebrated personalities:
Marshal Zhukov, pilots Pokryshkin and Kozhedub, aircraft engine designer
Mikulin, director Eisenstein, cardiac surgeon Amosov, weightlifter Vlasov and
many others whose innate art of paradoxical dialectical thinking helped them
"squeeze through" literally through the eye of a needle and win unpredictable
victories, make discoveries, achieve unexpected and unforeseen success in
seemingly unfavorable situations according to everyday consciousness. But Lenin
was by no means a spontaneous latent dialectician, whom there are countless
numbers of on planet Earth; rather, like Hegel, Marx and Engels, he undoubtedly
felt and realized himself as a dialectician and acted accordingly to the dialectical
nature of the world and the set of tools provided by this nature: not inventing
tools out of one's head, but discovering them using one's head [16, p. 148].
Accordingly, any conclusion drawn by Lenin is not arbitrariness or fabrication,
but a sober judgment based on careful study and meticulous analysis of the
established situation with identification of all the "actors and performers".
As mentioned above, through thinkers such as Marx, Hegel, Engels, Lenin,
nature itself (the surrounding world, developing reality) talks to us in the
language of pure dialectics. And our Vladimir Ilyich looks in this row of

 dialecticians even "cooler" than the aforementioned Germans, especially in
matters of practical implementation and embodiment of theoretical
developments.
Not only "Philosophical Notebooks" (compiled from quotes and notes made in
margins of books read) or “Materialism and Empiriocriticism” serve as evidence
of the author's deep understanding of the dialectical foundations of building and
harmony of the surrounding world, but any of his other works regardless of
content, and even solely on formal grounds, confirm his belonging to the ranks
of true conductors and tribunes of dialectics.
Why does Lenin's figure attract such close and lasting attention? Because he is
one of the greatest dialecticians of all times and peoples — a direct successor
and multiplier of the dialectical legacy of Hegel, Marx, Engels.
Lenin is so great and significant in terms of the practical application of the
mastery of dialectical thinking that none of the scientists and philosophers of all
stripes who lived after him and live today can currently be placed alongside him
in this respect. Brilliants of such size and cut appear once in hundreds of years.
Completely distancing ourselves from the heap of lies and absurdities expressed
about this outstanding thinker during the so-called "time of trouble" at the end of
the last century (let this remain entirely on the conscience of talkative
simpletons), we will assess the scale of Lenin's personality from the perspective
of the spirit and atmosphere of his theoretical works freely available: please, feel

With the expectation that this article may provide some support in mastering the
art of dialectical thinking (which is especially important for students of both
humanities and technical universities), we will demonstrate and reveal, using
Lenin's works as examples, the beauty and harmony of the dialectical method in
opposition to mechanistic, metaphysical, eclectic and scholastic ways of thinking.
Ultimately, what is important to know when studying various forms of reality:
object, process, phenomenon, etc.? It is essential to identify and track the logic,
historicism, trend, patterns, direction (i.e., the contentful side) of the
development of these forms of manifestation and existence of reality, for which it
turns out to be absolutely necessary to observe how transformation
(transmutation, conversion) of one form of reality into another takes place, and
furthermore, on this basis, try to forecast such transformations (transformations,
conversions), anticipating not only the change of existing forms but also the
emergence of new forms. This constitutes the subject matter of dialectics.
Ultimately, it comes down to studying the surrounding world (nature, man,
society) from the position of content-form transformations, transmutations,
conversions [2, 3, 7, 18].

 Every serious researcher, embarking on research work, proceeds from the
premise that reality (the surrounding world, nature) is always at least dual-sided
(i.e., double-faceted). Any real specific object, process or phenomenon in its
most general abstract form represents a relation of two principles (sides,
constituents, components, "opponents" etc.): {content/form}. Consequently,
any concrete form of reality (implying: object, process, phenomenon) is
determined by the correlation of these noted sides-constituents-components
within each of their specific relations. The development of forms of reality itself
represents changes in the correlations of these constituent-components within
their relations. In this connection it becomes obvious that forms of reality
defined by the aforementioned ratios can be either more or less Contentful (due
to different shares of content and formal components in their relations). The
overall trend of development and change of forms of reality — as human
observations throughout human history show — is such that during their (forms')
development there occurs a shift in the ratio of components (in their relations)
towards the numerator of the relation (if we consider such a relation as a
mathematical fraction), i.e., toward the Contentful component of the relation
(meaning the fundamental orientation toward the general movementdevelopment of forms of reality in the direction of increasing
their Contentfulness, and ultimately achieving ultimate highest Contentfulness)
[5, 7]. This setting-orientation indicating the direction of variability of all forms is
called the universal principle of self-development (self-organization) of reality,
formulated as follows: the development of the content of forms of reality takes
place in the direction of exhaustive expression of developing content by the very
same developing content of these forms [3, 5, 7, 18].
Applied to the surrounding world, this formulation means roughly the following:
everything that exists and develops has the direction of its development and
existence expressed (i.e., encompassed, absorbed, assimilated, comprehended,
etc.) by itself existing and developing. As a visual example in this case, the
image of a "self-winding" three-dimensional spiral seems most appropriate [2,
7]. And such an orientation or tendency of change-movement-development
belongs to all developing forms of reality without exception.
For greater illustrativeness of what was just said, note that with regard to such a
level (area) of developing reality as, say, man and society, this universal
principle drives forward not only positive (from the standpoint of human
consciousness) morally ethical and humanitarian aspirations of man but also
negative ones (again, in terms of human consciousness) — his thoughts,
motives, secret impulses and "sinful" inclinations — such as arrogance and
condescension, feelings of exclusivity and superiority over one's neighbour, envy
and vanity, etc., etc., Everyone intends and strains to present himself and
appear as the most significant, competent, respectable, successful, etc., in short
— the most contentful, which is also determined and conditioned by the same
universal objective striving of any forms for possession of the
highest contentfulness. After all, how sweet and tempting it is to participate in
some kind of political hangout and be considered in this world an influential
person — a disposer of human destinies!

 Thus, in light of the dialectical concept of development presented here,
objective reality represents motion and succession of its forms in the direction
of possessing the highest contentfulness (i.e., maximally achievable content),
and all processes of development and cognition of reality should be studied and
viewed through the prism of content-form transitions, transformations,
transmutations of unitary (i.e., strictly defined) directionality.
A specifically directed variability of the abstract relation {content/form} is
conditioned, on the one hand, by the unity and, on the other hand, non-identity
(non-sameness) of its components, due to which both components are in a state
of interaction and inexhaustible movement towards convergence with each other
and acquisition of equilibrium (balance) or mutual expressibility by each other
(which means: becoming maximally contentful for form and defining its perfect
form for content). The presence in one integral relation of two components with
different types of activity generates a whirlwind, vortex, circulation, "selfwinding" spiral, i.e., a specific type of change (movement, development) of both
components of this relation and the relation as a whole.
The famous saying of Heraclitus about everything flowing and changing still left
open the question of where exactly everything flows and changes — clear ideas
were lacking until now. Only today does the opportunity arise to answer this
question more or less sensibly; today we can meaningfully define the vector of
this universal movement: everywhere and always there is total multi-level
movement towards reaching the highest level of contentfulness; everything
is pervaded by the striving and covered by movement towards possession of the
highest contentfulness. This universal movement vector determines causality,
meanings and goals: life, development, evolution, history, etc., i.e., the
existence of anything whatsoever, in whatever forms.
The algorithm of development — common and universal for all levels-forms of
reality, from photon to the most elaborate conceptual schemes and constructions
in individual minds: new content will always strive to acquire a new form, while
forms seek to be filled, enriched with new content. Hence — a vortex-like motion
of everything. By this conception, only the typical, standard character of the
course and transformation of things at all levels is pointed out: the universal
generalized relation {content/form} is embodied on each specific level in its own
concrete form and consistently "proceeds" through levels towards replacing
relations with increasingly more contentful ones.
The movement or striving to achieve the highest contentfulness (as a single
goal for all changing forms of reality) conditions the fiercest rivalry and
competition between such moving and developing forms of reality. The inevitable
competition and rivalry arising from this movement (movement toward a
common finish line) manifests itself as confrontation, opposition and
interaction of real objects, processes and phenomena at different stages, in
different areas and at different levels of their existence-movement-development.

Being an entirely abstract construct, the relation {content/form} is
fundamentally not manifestable in its most general form or image, but it
nevertheless constitutes the core or very essence of any and every real concrete
form (object, process, phenomenon, etc.).
The noted duality of constituents-components of real forms-relations with a very
strict and definite directionality of content-form transformations during the
interaction of these constituents-components explains the moment-to-moment
uniqueness of the emerging world (Universe, nature, life, etc.) as a whole, as
well as the unique and unprecedented diversity of existing and nascent
forms as individual elements of this world.
The abstract relation {content/form} with quite unequivocal directionality of
change-movement-development of its components or constituents, just like the
entire relation as a whole, is something that exists originally, everywhere,
objectively and independently of any particular concreteness; it is what pervades
all existing and emerging concrete forms-levels-relations of surrounding reality
due to its omnipresence. It is precisely the content-form transformations
described above (i.e., changes of components and their relations in a strictly
defined direction — towards achieving the highest contentfulness) that underlie
the development of forms of reality, which are themselves only a concrete
embodiment and incarnation of the model presented above (i.e., the abstract
relation {content/form}). And it is exactly this initial model, owing to its
foundational and universality, that is most acceptable and effective for deep
study, research and penetration into the essence of the surrounding world
(developing reality) at the current stage of its development.
This investigative approach demonstrates its effectiveness through examples of
successful studies of issues that until recently were considered highly
problematic and "tricky" [5, 6].
Why do content-form relations suddenly come to the fore, become the core and
subject of examination and study of dialectics? Because the very fact and the
corresponding irrefutable assertion that there does not exist a single real object,
process or phenomenon devoid of content and/or formal sides-constituents
inevitably leads to the conclusion that content and form are those two
"principles" (two main key components, constituents, "opponents", etc.) which,

 interacting (opposing and simultaneously complementing each other) within the
unified integral relation {content/form}, create ("generate") and reproduce socalled objective reality, i.e., the entire surrounding world (including ourselves)
with all the diversity and uniqueness of its forms.
According to the textbook definition, dialectics is "the teaching about the most
general lawful connections and becoming, development of being and cognition,
and the method of creatively cognizing thinking based on this teaching... The
fundamental principles of dialectics, constituting its backbone, are universal
connection, becoming and development, which are conceptualized using the
entire historically established system of categories and laws" [15, p. 154].
The priority of the categories {content/form} over all others is obvious and
confirmed by the circumstance that in the foundation of all other categories and
concepts (just as of the actual objects, processes, phenomena of the physicalobjective level of reality denoted by these categories and concepts), one can
easily discover ubiquitous content-form beginnings-constituents-components.
It goes without saying and is undeniable that no one will ever be able to
encompass (i.e., comprehend) the entire volume of connections and the total
sum of changes occurring in all elements of the surrounding world (starting from
photons, including the abyss of atoms, molecules, living cells, etc., and ending
again with bizarre ideas and fantasies in the heads of individual human
individuals), but grasping and covering the trend or patterns of such changes
with human thought (from the standpoint of human thought or consciousness
itself) still turns out to be possible.
Here is what Lenin writes on this matter in his book “Materialism and
Empiriocriticism”, referring to just a relatively small segment of reality — the
global economy: "Each separate producer in the world economy is aware that he
introduces a certain change in production technique, each owner is aware that
he exchanges some products for others, but these producers and owners do not
realize that they thereby alter social being. No 70 Marxs could have covered
the sum of all these changes in all their ramifications in capitalist world
economy. At best, the laws of these changes have been discovered, the main
and basic objective logic of these changes and their historical development has
been shown... From the fact that you live and manage your affairs, give birth to
children and produce goods, exchange them, an objectively necessary chain of
events emerges, a chain of development independent of your public
consciousness, never fully comprehended by it. The highest task of
humanity is to grasp this objective logic of economic evolution
(evolution of social being) in general and basic terms in order to adapt
one's public consciousness to it as clearly, distinctly and critically as
possible..." [11, pp. 317–318].
Thus, the "objectively necessary chain of events" (including an objectively
necessary change in forms of economic management) determines or sets the
direction of change-movement-development-improvement of forms of human

With the destruction and loss of the USSR, Russia lost the prospects of its
further development previously outlined. Lenin and his comrades, being
deeply enlightened and educated people, clearly understood what the
formulation of goals and perspectives of movement-development meant for
an individual person and for a nation as a whole. Without formulating a goal
and prospect of development perceived and approved by the people, no
initiatives, initiative, enthusiasm can exist on a "mass scale". To unite and
organize the masses, public goals, directions and prospects of country
(state, society) development must be formulated according to which a
strategy for achieving these goals and prospects is developed. Moreover,
defining a perspective should not boil down to an immediate reaction to
external and internal so-called challenges and irritants but must be drawn up
taking into account long-term forecasts and strategic plans. Why did Lenin
and his like-minded associates understand this? Because the quality of
those country's leaders was immeasurable compared to today's; they were
people of a high level of consciousness and, respectively, personalities of
quite another scale.

An idea is based on feelings, continues them, but by no means reduces to

What was the contentfulness of that supposedly over-ideologized Soviet era?
What inspired, motivated the Soviet person to move forward?
The romance of everyday life was built on the dictate of the heart, energy of

from the need of the soul, man was ready to discover what had not been

 Two paths are known and possible for increasing, accumulating and multiplying
the own contentfulness (volume or fullness of content of one's own form):
1. Appropriation of someone else's content ("foreign" volumes, accumulations
of content belonging to other forms); as a particular case of this variant —
simple destruction (destruction, liquidation, neutralization) of an "adversarial"

2. Cooperation (symbiosis) with other forms and joint accumulation, increase of
content of each of the interacting and cooperating forms.
Needless to say, combinations of these two variants are significant.
Applied to the development of human communities, the essence of one and the

embryonic state; it was exactly this method of socialist construction and creation
of a new type of public order on a mass scale that V.I. Lenin advocated.
It is well-known (and confirmed beyond doubt by processes taking place during
the not-so-distant times of the breakup of the USSR) that initial capital
accumulation proceeds, as a rule, by violent and fraudulent means — by
appropriation and seizure.
We have all witnessed how the redistribution of public and state property,
capitals and assets took place in post-perestroika Russia and other republics of
the USSR that suddenly became "independent". This was a path of deceit,
swindling, gangster feuds, mockery of privatization coupons and pledge auctions.
The methods of executing this grand-scale fraud were, without any
exaggeration, predatory, and they relate entirely to the first path (variant) of
increasing contentfulness (i.e., enrichment) of the most active individual
reformers (young and not so young).
Undoubtedly, reverse expropriation of property and assets acquired in such a
manner also implies, to some extent, responsive violence at the initial stage of
building socialism. The retaliatory move is inevitably connected with
redistribution of once criminally appropriated or wrongly amassed "bourgeois"
property and financial assets, but this procedure is carried out in the interests of
the overwhelming majority of working population (citizens of the country) and
for the sake of restoring historical justice.

 As regards the legality of expropriation of property and capitals during times of
socialist revolutions, the procedure is performed, as already mentioned, in the
interests of the vast majority and is single-time (within a limited-short
timeframe); and whoever thinks that such procedures can be dispensed with at
periodic revolutionary iterations is deeply mistaken or simply ill-informed
regarding the inevitability of substantial transformation of current
foundations into the configuration of future public and governmental structure.
This stage is necessary, in particular, for redistributing initial capital in the
interests of the majority of the population in order to create normal starting
conditions (positions) for ordinary workers and to restore a justified balance with
the positions of aggressively pushy and shameless (for the most part) minority
that once usurped assets not belonging to them.
Yes, development proceeds, and history is written "by tacks", zigzags — every
time returning to itself at a new level by segments of spiral turns that never fully
line up and are never perfectly finished. Such is the external appearance and
character of the dialectical mode of development of anything whatsoever.
Somewhere again forced measures of expropriation will be needed, because
otherwise it just won't work: nobody ever voluntarily surrenders what was
gained in the sweat of others' brows and appropriated in the sweat of
one's own brow. One must be quite naive and unschooled in practical life not
to understand this.
In contrast to the first path, implementing the second option for increasing
the contentfulness of real forms of public order means immersion into
socialism, toward which man is increasingly pushed by emerging
circumstances regardless of his consciousness; and we will have to revive
and continue this path whether we like it or not because
further contentful development of mankind outside of this path is
unprofitable, suboptimal, inefficient, "dead-end" and therefore unlikely. And
deeper study of socialist theory will be required. And again, one will have to
acknowledge the fairness and scientific nature of Marx's approach applied in
working out social and economic theories (otherwise, gentlemen courtiersapologists of today's socio-economic foundations, you will simply lose your
target "fan" audiences and, as a consequence, your piece of bread; then
there will come time to laugh good-naturedly at those who arrogantly
mocked the orthodoxy of Marxism and indulged in primitivism of scientific
communism — well, sirs, he laughs best who laughs last).
Following Lenin's methods and research tools, we can state today that thanks
to applying the dialectical approach or method of cognition, much of what is
called world order becomes clearer than before. At the same time, the stillrelevant task does not diminish but rather stands out even more clearly: to
keep learning how to see the future picture more accurately (i.e., learn to
look ahead "around the corner" with ever greater efficiency) so as to
understand ourselves and surrounding reality better.

 Solving this problem is identical to solving the eternal issue of finding
meaning in life for every individual person, which (solution), in its first
approximation, takes on the following form: everything existing moves in a
single direction towards expressing objective truth in its most contentful,

undoubtedly belongs not only to any separate individual but also to whole

best. Following the course towards achieving the highest contentfulness by
forms of developing reality (including humanity) is also a movement towards
effective resolution of the perennially troubling human question regarding the

What is life, motion, development, progress, etc., in general terms is already
understood: it is a process of contentful filling of forms while striving for
them (at all levels without exception) to possess the highest
(objective) contentfulness. It is a process of "unleashing" the inner content of
reality and presenting it outwardly in the most contentful form possible at
any given moment, approaching each time the form of exhaustive expression
of objective truth. With small acts of subjective human movements (whether
achievements in painting, literature, music, sports, science, etc.) humankind
approaches closer to the fullest expression of the objective content of
developing reality (expression of objective truth) with each such
elementary act. Every sound, every note produced by a skilled musician or
composer seeks to bring to light and reveal to the world objective truth —
i.e., the most contentful form of representation of reality at that particular
moment (from the viewpoint of the maestro). The same applies to poetic
word or brushstroke on an artist's canvas, let alone the contentful theories
and concepts of a scientist. From the most contentful subjective
opinions and views on the world, objective truth is formed [5].
But understanding and awareness of the general trend of real processes by
no means exhausts the solution of all current issues: the crucial and essential
question for man remains open forever — the question of anticipating,
foreseeing, preempting, predicting with maximum accuracy and certainty
changes (variability) of existing forms of reality and emergence (appearance)
of new ones, and taking into account this circumstance — the question of
planning subsequent human activity. Well, and since man by his very
nature and place in the chain of development is a highly active linkcomponent (in other words — subject of activity), he inevitably interferes
with the development of reality and embodies thereby his own vision,
understanding and "plans", impacting the surrounding world and changing it
in the direction required by him (strictly in accordance with the
aforementioned universal principle of self-development).
Despite our ability to define the meaning of life and existence both for man
and his entire environment today (see above), the matter still lies in learning

 to anticipate the change of existing forms of reality and the appearance of
new ones, in order to predict events and developments as precisely as
possible, to learn to peer deeper into the future — and not just to satisfy
immediate curiosity, but mainly to survey and outline distant prospects.
Development is the succession of forms of reality aimed at creating and
establishing forms filled with higher objective content. All ongoing processes
in the surrounding world are "targeted" at enhancing the contentfulness of
existing forms representing changing reality. In this lies the essence of the
orientation of transformation of nature in the universal cosmic dimension.
The search for, acquisition, comprehension of truth, i.e., discovering the
most contentful forms of representation or acquiring developing objective
content, permeates all of nature — from living thinking beings (with their
specific subforms in the guise of ideal abstract constructs of thought) to an
inanimate stone-boulder, and any molecule, atom, electron, photon
(quantum) within this stone or beyond it. And no empty speculations on this
score, embodying former "highbrow" (sophistical, demagogic, speculative,
scholastic, etc.) philosophy, are probably needed anymore, since they turn
out to be low-contentful and therefore fruitless. Philosophy gradually changes
its status and role, turning from a habitual tool of passively descriptive and
explanatory type into an instrument of actively prognostic, predictive and
transformative character. Its speculative nature, conditioned by centuries-old
intrigues or games of idle human mind, finally turns itself into an
uninteresting useless "thingie", a whimsically intricate relic of the past.
Dialectics comes forward as the core and embodiment of a new, deeper
philosophy, as the art of generating and bringing to life correct forecasts and
planned transformations conceived by man. And here our updated philosophy
meets its inevitable merger and fusion with science, as was excessively
discussed throughout the 20th century.
Summarizing the above in two words, we have every reason to draw the
following conclusion: to learn to understand and know how to see the
perspective of development of reality, i.e., the perspective
(orientation) of change of its (reality's) existing forms and
emergence (appearance) of new ones, and on this basis plan
subsequent human activity — this is the main task facing the man of the
future, worthy of investing any resources for its gradual step-by-step
resolution.
The socialist idea is closest, most responsive to the very spirit of the Russian
person, whose essence since time immemorial has been considered an
inexhaustible craving (aspiration) for justice. Truly popular can only be the
power that professes exactly this idea; when a working person can feel with
every cell of his that this is his native people's power — then he will defend it,
and cherish it, and nurture it, and improve the institutions of power, and invest
with enthusiasm his strength and energy into "arranging" life. But if we have
given the land, its subsoil, national wealth and means of production into the

 hands of "scoundrels", allowed them to fence themselves off from the people
with high fences and armed security regarding all this primordially people's
property — then where can unity for the sake of a common goal come from —
no matter how you "blur" the eyes of your fellow citizens with pharisaic slogans
about the supposedly "national property".
The craving for justice inherent in every Russian person and, as a derivative of
this property of the soul, the aspiration to save one's neighbor are conditioned
by his natural inclination to search for and find balance (equilibrium) both inside
and on the outer contour of society in opposition to encroachments (aggression)
on freedom and dignity both at the level of an individual person and at the level
of human communities.
The social orientation of the state or public structure in this case should be
determined by the officially proclaimed policy of the state, not by charity,
assistance, petty handouts, voluntary donations or patronage timidly pushed
through from time to time and on the sly. Of course, a state of this type must be
built on principles other than the existing ones.
It is necessary to return to the working person the feeling of involvement in a
great cause, a great people, a great country with its innumerable natural
resources and national wealth; return the feeling of involvement in a great
common goal, most effectively approached by joint efforts using socialized
means of production. When there is such a feeling, which in turn revives and
nourishes feelings of human pride and dignity, — then a person is ready to give
himself entirely to the common cause, which inevitably becomes the personal
cause of everyone. We must return to our people the lost sense of selfworth inherent in the Soviet man.
Does the first tentative approach to mastering the socialist idea mean the
complete collapse of Marxism, Leninism, theories of socialism and scientific
communism, etc., as primitive and short-sighted politicians, political scientists,
philosophers, economists believe? Of course not! Humanity will return to such
fundamental currents and theories more than once, approaching them in a
spiral-cyclical way (or by successive approximations) — in full accordance with
the nature and character of the content-form (dialectical) movementdevelopment of reality — to an increasingly exhaustive version of their
implementation. And something here suggests that the point of view of the wise
classics of Marxism is not devoid of grounds and will, in the end, prevail in the
structure of searching for the optimal path of mankind's development, since it
most fully corresponds to the inner content of man, his mood, oriented towards
preserving human identity, culture, traditions, dignity (accordingly to genetic
predisposition, genetic matrix, genetic code and the so-called call of ancestors
and blood). According to the formulation of the principle of self-development,
everything existing and developing periodically returns "to its own circle", but in
other, more contentful and enriched forms.

 Dialectics is the art of finding balance of interacting sides, which (art) Lenin
possessed impeccably and perfectly. For Lenin — it is always a result-oriented
search for the optimal correlation between the most essential sides-constituentscomponents of development (in their relation): in the range, for example, from
de-kulakization and surplus-appropriation to the introduction of a food tax and
NEP, or from asserting total collective ownership of the means of production to
establishing and recognizing as relevant a mode of production with elements of
private property, etc. In this regard, first of all, his ability to find and highlight
the most essential sides-constituents of reality, being in direct interaction and
relation to each other (i.e., in live confrontation and opposition) precisely at this
particular segment of their development, and already on this basis — to
demonstrate the ability to forecast the trend of change in the correlation of
identified sides, and along with this — to anticipate the further course and
perspective of development of the entire relation as a whole. And it looks
absolutely fantastic to be able to identify sources of renewal (inflow, increase,
receipt) of Contentful energy in pairs of interacting components and further — to
anticipate and track the bias of content-form transformations (transmutations) of
these components and their relations as a whole.
It is on considering issues similar to those touched upon above that we will
focus, studying and analyzing the works of V.I. Lenin from the standpoint of their
being imbued with the spirit of dialectics.
Any article or work of Lenin is a dynamic creation, structured according to a
universal scheme corresponding to the dialectical nature of the development of
reality itself (i.e., according to the scheme of tracking the change-movement of
interacting forms towards achieving their highest contentfulness): the variability
of the correlation of two interacting sides-components in their relation is
investigated with subsequent forecasting of the development of the result of this
interaction towards (into the area) of predominant increase in
the contentfulness of the active component and the relation as a whole.
Compositionally and structurally it looks something like this.

Forecasting of event development: on the basis of the assessment
