on an oligarchic type (scheme): first money is made (and capital is
accumulated), then power is desired in the name of new opportunities and
new money, and the combination of both again multiplies power and money.
For a person with an unprepared, immature, undeveloped consciousness —
this is a dead end, a closed vicious circle, a trap. A corrupt capitalist country
is always an oligarchic state. On the other hand, the management
configuration that has developed in the country today is quite accurately
determined by the term "plutocracy". On the third hand, this is, of course,
also an "autocracy", represented by the "face" of the current "ruler". Before
us is such a volatile mixture of plutocratic, oligarchic and autocratic elements
of statehood. In this infrastructure, where there is everything and a lot of it,
there is only one small link missing — the rule of the people; the working
people simply do not "fit" with the modern government and
therefore are not represented in the government].
There are assurances that "the recognition of the right to secession increases the
danger of the state's disintegration. ... From the point of view of democracy in
general, it is quite the opposite: the recognition of the right to secession reduces
the danger of the "disintegration of the state"" [8, p. 592].

 Further, the question is examined using the example of the Ukrainian
nationality: "Is it not clear that the more freedom the Ukrainian nationality has in
one or another country, the stronger the connection of this nationality with the
given country will be? It seems that one cannot argue against this ABC truth if
one does not decisively break with all the premises of democratism. And can
there be greater freedom of a nationality as such than the freedom of secession,
the freedom of forming an independent national state?" [8, p. 592].
[At first glance, it may seem incorrect that the dialectical position, according to
which the recognition of the right of nations to self-determination does not
increase the danger of the state's disintegration, but on the contrary, cements
the country and strengthens the ties between nationalities — since in relation to,
say, the above-mentioned Ukrainian nationality, this dialectical position was not
fulfilled and is not being fulfilled. However, in this particular case, the following
circumstances should be taken into account. Unlike the conditions and events
corresponding to the temporary stage analyzed in the book by Lenin we are
considering, for some time now (already in our times), under the patronage of
the local "comprador" oligarchy, on the territory once called the Ukrainian SSR, a
shoot of rabid nationalism and fierce hatred of everything Russian, cultivated in
the deep past and pulled out from the dilapidated sewer outlets, has bloomed in
full bloom. From this perspective, the revived phenomenon already falls under
the definition not of a traditional national liberation movement (acquiring
freedom and the right of a nation to self-determination), but of aggressive
Nazism based on blood feud and innate hatred (the roots of which must be
sought in the origin of the once artificially bred and carefully selected "marginal"
nationalism), the formation of which has little in common with a national
liberation movement. Extremely interesting in this regard is the fact that from a
whole range of levels-forms within the composition of their multi-level totality
(uniting in itself diverse methods of interethnic interaction), the lowest, most
primitive level receives an impetus for priority development (under the
"management" of the same universal principle of Self-development) in the image
of some fanged horned creature with a tail and fur that has not yet fallen off,
crawled out of a dark deep cave to teach the whole civilized world its
understanding of life and interethnic communication. Like a weed stifling
cultivated plants at the root, this primitive "misunderstanding" is capable for
some time of diverting to itself and "grinding" the contentful volumes worked out
later, but already tested, or, simply put, absorbing (destroying) the civilized
forms of higher levels. Such are the curiosities and "inscrutable" paths of the
dialectical development of diverse forms-levels of reality].
As for the attitude to the national question, for example, of Marx: "Marx makes
no absolute of national movements, knowing that the complete liberation of all
nationalities can only be given by the victory of the working class. To take into
account in advance all possible correlations between the bourgeois liberation
movements of oppressed nations and the proletarian liberation movement
among the oppressing nation (this is precisely the problem that makes the
national question so difficult in modern Russia) is an impossible thing" [8, p.
608].

 [In other words, one must support the oppressed nation in its struggle and direct
this struggle towards facilitating the proletarian movement, since the analysis of
all variants of correlations (line-up of forces) between the forces of national
liberation and proletarian movements (in their relation) is impossible even with
the involvement of the intellectual power of 70 Marxs (to use Lenin's words, who
always meant the constant presence of some objective uncertainty in the
development of certain forms-relations and the impossibility of knowing or
anticipating the development of these forms with one hundred percent
certainty). As we can see, the ability to think dialectically allowed the classics of
Marxism, and in particular V.I. Lenin, to focus attention by no means on
obtaining exhaustive knowledge about the outcome of the interaction of the
studied components, but only on understanding the tendency of variability of
their relations, in order to already on this basis forecast the further development
of their forms].
"The protocols of the congress of 1903 [II Congress of the RSDLP], which
adopted the program [of the party] of Russian Marxists, have become the
greatest rarity, and the vast majority of modern figures of the workers'
movement are not familiar with the motives of individual points of the program.
...Let us note first of all that, however scanty the Russian Social-Democratic
literature concerning the "right of nations to self-determination" may be, it is
nevertheless absolutely clear from it that this right was always understood in the
sense of the right to secession.
...The reader sees that at the II Congress of the party, which adopted the
program, there were not two opinions on the question that self-determination
means "only" the right to secession" [8, pp. 610-611, 613].
"...The right to secession presupposes the solution of the question
precisely not by the central parliament, but only by the parliament
(sejm, referendum, etc.) of the seceding region" [8, p. 617].
"Great Russian nationalism, like any nationalism, goes through various phases
[i.e., this question, like any other, Lenin considers through the prism of historical
development: from having a hard autocratic reactionary color to appearing in the
color of bourgeois liberalism], depending on the predominance [i.e., on the bias
and shift towards a more substantial, more contentful component in their
relation — in this case in the relation {bourgeois national-liberalism/autocratic
monarchic national-reactionism}] of one or another class in a bourgeois country.
Before 1905, we knew almost only national-reactionaries. After the revolution of
1905, national-liberals were born among us. And further, the birth of Great
Russian national-democrats is inevitable" [8, p. 619].
"From the point of view of the theory of Marxism in general, the question of the
right to self-determination presents no difficulties. There can seriously be no talk

 either of challenging the London decision of 1896, or of the fact that by selfdetermination is meant only the right to secession, or of the fact that the
formation of independent national states is a tendency of all bourgeoisdemocratic upheavals.
The difficulty is created to a certain extent by the fact that in Russia the
proletariat of oppressed nations and the proletariat of the oppressing nation are
fighting and must fight side by side. To defend the unity of the class struggle of
the proletariat for socialism, to repel all bourgeois and Black-Hundred influences
of nationalism — this is the task. Among the oppressed nations, the separation
of the proletariat into an independent party sometimes leads to such a fierce
struggle with the nationalism of a given nation that the perspective is distorted
and the nationalism of the oppressing nation is forgotten" [8, pp. 617-618].
"The slower the democratic transformation of Russia goes, the more persistent,
rough, and fierce will be the national persecution and squabbling of the
bourgeoisie of different nations. ...Full equality of nations; the right of nations to
self-determination; the merging of workers of all nations — this national
program teaches workers Marxism, teaches the experience of the whole world
and the experience of Russia" [8, p. 620].
[Analyzing the above, one can be convinced that the slogan in defense of the
right of nations to self-determination is always relevant — since it is an indicator
of the recognition of the equality of all small and large nations in a multinational
state (which, undoubtedly, should serve as the main condition for the cohesion
of nations in union states); in case of legalizing this right, it is easier for the
oppressed classes to defeat any oppressor, uniting on the basis of equality of all
nations.
True equality of nations is conditioned and ensured only by the recognition of the
right of nations to self-determination (political self-determination, i.e. possible
and permissible secession). This principle of self-determination is relevant for
Russia (as it was relevant for the USSR) also because its peoples, like the
peoples of the USSR, united and entered unions, as a rule, with their territories
— i.e., not being newcomers or immigrants, which cannot be said, for example,
about the USA and a number of other states.
But all this was accepted with delight and looked exactly like that until the right
of nations to self-determination enshrined in the constitution suddenly served as
a reason for merciless accusations of destroying a great country. It goes without
saying that the main claims were made against the founder of the first socialist
state in the world, Vladimir Ilyich Lenin, who allegedly "laid" a delayed-action
"mine" under the Soviet Union.

Advancing such accusations, no one even remotely thinks about the objective
possibility of an unfavorable (from the point of view of human plans and

 hopes) course and outcome of content-form transformations, which always
take place in the process of reality development. No one thinks about the
inevitability of content-form transformations, conversions, transfigurations to
which any developing form is subjected in the process of "making itself out of
itself". In this case, it was only required to be a very well-informed and
competent leader to always remember the objectivity of the tendency of
natural transfiguration of forms into their opposite, i.e. about the immanent
dialectical property (character) of developing reality, described by the
formulation of the universal principle of self-development (see above).
Nevertheless, the real state of affairs is such that by virtue of this very
dialectical nature of the surrounding world, everything (without exception)
sooner or later has a habit of returning "to its own circle", but not in its
former form, but in other — "modified" — forms. In case of misunderstanding
such a layout or in case of inept and imprudent handling of the mentioned
modified forms — the impacts, and even blows of these weighted returning
forms may fall not where the lower back is (it would be fine if it were so,
which is still tolerable), but where the neck is higher.
Having detected such a trend manifesting in connection with the
development of one or another form of reality, one can and should learn (if
necessary) to influence this trend, preventing or anticipating the emergence
of undesirable (from the point of view of human consciousness)
consequences, which, naturally, no one in those times fulfilled not only was
not, but was not even supposed to be fulfilled — after all, the last
outstanding dialectician in the chain of responsible persons turned out to be
Lenin, and all his other followers and continuators, from the point of view of
dialectical training, are neither here nor there (ne prishey kobyle khvost).
However, to blame, in all troubles and failures, the one who understands
such issues best — this is in our days (as, indeed, always) a downright sign
of good manners. Having an idea of the inevitable transformation or
transfiguration of changing forms into their opposites (i.e., about returning
"to one's own circle"), in order to keep these forms within the framework of
their former status, it is necessary in various ways to increase
their contentfulness (in this case — literacy, education, awareness, etc.).
Perhaps, one cannot even think of a more vivid example in confirmation of
the urgent need to master the art of dialectical thinking, dialectical
research approach and practical activity!
In the USSR, at the stage of swaying and the so-called "perestroika", the
party nomenclature (the forerunner of the emerging bourgeoisie) of precisely
"aliens", i.e. national formations (republics), finally went out of the control of
the central authority, which determined the collapse of the great Union.
Starting from the Khrushchev times, and especially during the Gorbachev
perestroika time, obvious and covert decomposition, de-ideologization and
transfiguration of both central (union) and local (republican), in modern
slang, "elites" (or rather, pseudo-elites — party nomenclature, top and
middle managers, heads of large enterprises, etc.) was in full swing, which

 were swiftly becoming "philistinized" and "bourgeoisified", turning into their
own ideologically contentless (but filled with bourgeois-mercantilist content)
opposite in full accordance with the dialectical character of reality
development. As is proper in such "non-transparent" cases (i.e., in times of
turmoil), the contentful cause of what is happening is pushed to the
background and its place is "draped" with the Formal component of the real
process. In the established relation {nomenclature power in the localities /
formal arrangement of local power based on the right of nations to political
secession}, due to the sharp spontaneous-uncontrolled expansion of the
powers and capabilities of the nomenclature local power (i.e., the "swelling"
of the contentful component or the "numerator" of the above-mentioned
relation), the "denominator" of the relation also begins to change — towards
isolation or separation from the center and the dominance of the
nomenclature local pseudo-elite (power structures).
The correctness and validity of the idea of the right of nations to selfdetermination even at that moment is beyond any doubt provided that strict
control is ensured over other particulars and details. The motives and actions
of the nomenclature of "aliens" (using the terminology of Lenin's articles),
which, having found itself without "supervision and care", played its
mercantilist card to the victorious end, which could have been decisively
suppressed on quite legal grounds, should have been put under control.
Illegal actions of the decaying nomenclature at the level of republican
authorities should have been stopped, relying on the "Constitution (Basic
Law) of the USSR" and on the then still functional central and republican
structures of law enforcement agencies: KGB, MVD, MO (Chekists, police,
army), continuing to keep ideology and personnel policy under control. And,
as we now know for sure, due to the lack of such control and
countermeasures, the internal decomposition of the pseudo-elite ends, in the
end, with its transformation into an oligarchy of central and local significance
(scale); and, of course, not without external foreign influence and complicity.
Unprincipled and unscrupulous nouveau riche nomenclature figures in
conjunction with inveterate bandits and criminals became the new masters of
life.
Yes, the decisions (and actions) of the local pseudo-elites formally fell under
the patronage of the constitutional right of nations to self-determination, but
these decisions were not legal from the point of view of confirmation by the
officially identified will of the majority of citizens of the national republics.
The legality of actions was replaced by "under-the-table" activity and the
pushiness of local nomenclature structures and individuals. Thus, not the
notorious right of nations to self-determination became the cause of the
destruction of the USSR, but the dominance that had developed by that time
of the satiated, transfigured de-ideologized "comprador" (venal) top and the
lack of control over its behavior.

 Thus (it is emphasized specifically for the current "rulers" and their ilk), Ilyich
did not "lay" any "mines" in the arrangement of the multinational Soviet
state — all decisions of the Bolsheviks were conditioned by the specific
context of the epoch experienced and there is nothing to blame him for the
alleged lack of foresight; in our opinion, the current "armchair" opponents
and experts should read his works more attentively and thoughtfully and not
rush to proclaim their own mental superiority. The very raising of the
question of the alleged "laid mine" testifies to an insufficiently high level of
intelligence and education of the persons raising this issue, since the
question regarding the "exhaustion" or discovered over time "nonoperability" of this decision should not be asked of Lenin, who, we repeat,
knew how to skillfully draw conclusions and make decisions in accordance
with the circumstances of a certain time stage, but with those persons who,
due to the rigidity of their thinking, could not subsequently flexibly react to
changing conditions. The role and significance of the human factor (and
personnel policy), ladies and gentlemen, no one has yet canceled. Again,
without possessing a dialectical mindset, it is oh so difficult to search for and
find correct solutions to the most complex questions — which pushes (forces)
ordinary incompetent persons (including superficial researchers) to
shamelessly attribute all mistakes and miscalculations to extraordinary,
but, unfortunately, humble and silent predecessors.
It is quite probable that in our days a variant of establishing a union association
could be more productive, in which any national formation (republic, state,
autonomy) would enter the composition of a new federal arrangement on the
rights of a territorial district with the same "right to self-determination", but not
on a national, but on a territorial basis and with the obligation to establish a
single citizenship for the entire population as an indicator of belonging to the
common state structure (well, naturally, and with all other attributes of a single
state: a single currency, common goals, a single defense doctrine and law
enforcement agencies, etc.). But this is still a question requiring the involvement
of dialectical minds for its effective solution, who would be able to track the
peripeteia of the changing situation and accordingly adjust the decisions made
throughout the entire period of the relevance of this issue. God forbid the current
"rulers" should imagine themselves to be qualified "resolvers" of national
problems, and on this wave get involved in defusing the "mines" allegedly "laid"
by Lenin. Without taking into account the numerous nuances of the national
question, these "resolvers", not being skilled dialecticians for a single time, will
make a mess and out of ignorance or lack of foresight will finally bury a big
country under this firewood.
In any case, a simple solution to the national question by means of the so-called
"melting pot", from which serious racial problems, still not even close to being
resolved, suddenly crawled out (as the American near-election crisis of 2020
shows), is also impossible, which should be taken into account by all primitive
figures and flat "resolvers" when they assume to close the sore topic once and
for all in this way.

 Meanwhile, this issue remains extremely topical at least because the sovereignty
(and, consequently, the identity) of a small nation (for example, the people of
Belarus in modern conditions) can be ensured and preserved on the principles of
the right of a nation to self-determination only if it exists (functions) in symbiosis
with a large (predominant in population) nation (within or under the wing of a
united Russia or an updated, modernized USSR, for example), which guarantees
this sovereignty and undertakes to protect the small nation from attacks and
claims from aggressive capitalist neighbors; otherwise, as the practice of today
shows, the aspiration (as a temptation) of a small (unself-sufficient) state to
pursue its own independent policy (adherence to the so-called political multivector approach) will sooner or later turn this state into an appendage of more
powerful capitalist states with inevitable leveling (nullification) of its national
identity. In fact, the analysis of Lenin's vision of the development options of this
topic leads precisely to such a conclusion.]
2. The manifesto "War and Russian Social-Democracy" [8, pp. 622-628],
published in November 1914, was the first official document of the RSDLP, which
outlined the position of the Bolshevik party regarding the beginning of the world
imperialist war.
"The European war, which for decades had been prepared by the governments
and bourgeois parties of all countries, broke out. ... Seizure of lands and
subjugation of foreign nations, ruin of a competing nation, plunder of its wealth,
diversion of the attention of the working masses from the internal political crises
of Russia, Germany, England and other countries, disunity and nationalist duping
of workers and the extermination of their vanguard for the purpose of weakening
the revolutionary movement of the proletariat — such is the only real content,
significance and meaning of the modern war" [8, p. 622].
[At the beginning of the article, Lenin analyzes the current situation and the
alignment of forces, showing that at the head of one of the warring groups
stands the German bourgeoisie, assuring the working class that it is waging a
war for the defense of the homeland, freedom and culture, for the liberation of
the peoples oppressed by tsarism and the destruction of reactionary tsarism, but
in fact being a faithful ally of tsarism and the enemy of the revolutionary
movement of workers and peasants in Russia and supporting the tsarist
monarchy against the revolution in Russia. At the head of the other group of
warring nations stands the English and French bourgeoisie, duping the working
class and the working masses, claiming that it is waging a war for the homeland,
freedom and culture against militarism and despotism of Germany, but in fact
striving to seize German colonies and ruin a competing nation, distinguished by
faster economic development. Contentful enrichment (accumulation of the
content of one's own form) at the expense of others, at the expense of
competitors — this is the meaning of this war (division, redistribution and seizure
of markets, destruction of competitors). In other words, the attitudes of lower
(i.e., more primitive) levels-forms towards multiplying their contentfulness by
taking away and consuming "alien" content overcome or take precedence over
the socialist attitudes or goals of more developed levels, professing the
accumulation and increase of their contentfulness through joint creative labor,

 conducting research of developing reality by common forces, cognition and
forecasting by joint efforts of the emergence of new forms of reality at all levels,
as well as directions of prospective human activity].
"Both groups of belligerent countries do not yield to each other in robberies,
atrocities and endless cruelties of war, but in order to dupe the proletariat and
divert its attention from the only truly liberating war, namely the civil war
against the bourgeoisie of both "their" country and "foreign" countries, for this
high purpose the bourgeoisie of each country with false phrases about patriotism
tries to exalt the significance of "its" national war and assure that it seeks to
defeat the enemy not for robbery and land seizure, but for the "liberation" of all
other peoples, except its own.
...But the more diligently the governments and the bourgeoisie of all countries
try to disunite the workers and set them against each other... — the more
urgent is the duty of the conscious proletariat to defend its class cohesion, its
internationalism, its socialist convictions against the rampage of chauvinism of
the "patriotic" bourgeois clique of all countries. To refuse this task would mean
on the part of the conscious workers to refuse all their liberating and democratic,
not to mention socialist, aspirations.
With the deepest bitterness, it has to be stated that the socialist parties of the
main European countries did not fulfill this task of theirs, and the behavior of the
leaders of these parties — especially the German one — borders on direct
betrayal of the cause of socialism. At the moment of the greatest world-historical
importance, the majority of the leaders of the current, second (1889–1914)
Socialist International are trying to replace socialism with nationalism. Due to
their behavior, the workers' parties of these countries did not oppose themselves
to the criminal behavior of the governments, but called the working class to
merge their position with the position of the imperialist governments. The
leaders of the International committed treason in relation to socialism, voting for
war credits, repeating the chauvinistic ("patriotic") slogans of the bourgeoisie of
"their" countries, justifying and defending the war, entering the bourgeois
ministries of the warring countries, etc., etc. The most influential socialist leaders
and the most influential organs of the socialist press of modern Europe stand on
a chauvinistic-bourgeois and liberal [by the way, nothing has fundamentally
changed since then], by no means on a socialist point of view. The responsibility
for this disgrace of socialism falls primarily on the German Social-Democrats,
who were the strongest and most influential party of the Second International"
[8, pp. 623-624].
"The collapse of the Second International is the collapse of opportunism
[apostasy and conciliation], which was cultivated on the soil of the features of
the past (the so-called "peaceful") historical epoch and gained actual domination
in the International in recent years. The opportunists had long been preparing
this collapse, denying the socialist revolution and replacing it with bourgeois
reformism; denying the class struggle with its necessary transformation at
certain moments into a civil war and preaching class cooperation...

 ...It is impossible to fulfill the tasks of socialism at the present time, it is
impossible to realize the real international cohesion of workers without a decisive
break with opportunism and explaining to the masses the inevitability of its
fiasco.
[In other words, the war and the inability of the European social-democrats to
resist the bourgeoisie, their conciliation with the slogans of the bourgeoisie
testify to the collapse of the Second International, which Lenin proposes not to
hush up, but on the contrary, to recognize and emphasize. Without demarcation
from such a position of the bourgeoisie, it is impossible to fulfill the tasks of

4. The article "On the Slogan of the United States of Europe" [8, pp.
633-636] was written in August 1915. It deals with the incorrectness
(untimeliness) of this slogan in the economic aspect. If in the political aspect
this slogan, put in connection with the revolutionary overthrow of the three
most reactionary monarchies of Europe (German, Austrian and Russian), is
completely invulnerable, there remains the most important question about
the economic content and significance of this slogan. "From the point of view
of the economic conditions of imperialism, i.e. the export of capital and the
division of the world by "advanced" and "civilized" colonial powers, the United
States of Europe under capitalism is either impossible or reactionary", since
"it amounts to an agreement on the division of colonies" [8, pp. 634635].
Capital has become international and monopolistic; the world is divided
among a handful of "great powers" succeeding in great robbery and
oppression of nations. In the era of the highest development of capitalism, a
handful of great powers have organized the robbery of about a billion of the
Earth's population. [Isn't this relevant today, and even to a greater extent?
You read Lenin's article more than a century old, and it seems as if it is
written about our time!]. A different organization (i.e. voluntary renunciation
of colonies, spheres of influence, export of capital) is impossible under
capitalism, as are a different basis and a different principle of division, except
for force. Capitalism is private ownership of the means of production and the
anarchy of production. To preach a "fair" division of income on such a basis is
the dull-wittedness of a philistine. A billionaire cannot share income with
anyone else otherwise than in proportion "according to capital". Hence — it
cannot be divided otherwise than "by force" [i.e. by force methods]. And
force changes with the course of economic development, and to check the
actual force of a developing capitalist state, there is and can be no other
means except war. Under capitalism [due to the anarchy and spontaneity of
market production], uniform growth of economic development of individual
farms and individual states is impossible, and therefore under capitalism
there are no other means of restoring from time to time the disturbed
equilibrium and eliminating disproportions than crises in industry and
wars in politics. War is not in contradiction with the foundations of private
property, but is a consequence of the direct and inevitable development of

 these foundations (i.e. the need for periodic revision and redistribution of the
accumulations of private property).
Thus, based on what has been said on the modern economic basis, i.e. under
capitalism, the United States of Europe would mean the organization of
reaction to delay the faster development of America. The times when the
cause of democracy and the cause of socialism were connected only with
Europe have passed irrevocably. Under such conditions, the slogan "United
States of the World" would be more correct and relevant, however, it could
give rise to an incorrect interpretation of the question in the impossibility of
the victory of socialism in one country [8, p. 636].
The unevenness of economic and political development is an absolute law of
capitalism. It follows from this that the victory of socialism is possible initially
in a few or even in one single capitalist country. The political form of society
in which the proletariat wins, overthrowing the bourgeoisie, will be a
democratic republic, increasingly centralizing the forces of the proletariat of a
given nation or given nations in the struggle against states that have not yet
transitioned to socialism. On the basis of the foregoing, Lenin comes to the
conclusion (makes a diagnosis) about the impossibility of destroying
classes without the dictatorship of the oppressed class and the
impossibility of the free unification of nations in socialism without a more or
less long, persistent struggle of socialist republics with backward states. By
virtue of these considerations, a conclusion is made about the incorrectness
of the slogan of the United States of Europe at this particular historical
moment [8, p. 636], since it will be expressed in the postponement of the
beginning of the socialist revolution.

5. The article "The Military Program of the Proletarian Revolution" [8,
pp. 751-761] was written in German in September 1916, and was printed
only a year later. Then it was intended for Swiss, Swedish and Norwegian left
Social-Democrats. The publication was preceded by the following foreword:
"Nowadays, when Lenin is one of those figures of the Russian revolution who
are most often spoken about, the following article of this old iron
revolutionary, outlining a significant part of his political program, is of
particular interest" [8, p. 834]. In the Russian language in Russia, this work
was first published only in 1929.
Structurally and compositionally, the article is built according to the same very
typical stencil: analysis of the current situation (state of affairs); identification of
the interacting sides in their relation, both old and new (transformed and
developed); determination of the active, leading, leading component in these
relations, especially in the new one; forecasting the direction of variability of
both the components-constituents themselves in this new relation and the
relation as a whole.
The appearance of this article was caused by the circumstance that along with
the justified and fair opposition to the false slogan of the social-chauvinists about
the "defense of the fatherland" in the ongoing imperialist war, voices began to be
heard in favor of replacing the old point of the Social-Democratic program
"arming of the people" (formation of a "militia") with the new point
"disarmament".
"The main argument is that the demand for disarmament is the most consistent
expression of the struggle against all militarism and against any war." But in this
argument lies the main fallacy of the supporters of disarmament: socialists,

 without ceasing to be socialists, cannot be against any war, and in particular a
revolutionary war, a national liberation war, a civil war (as well as the so-called
"defensive" wars of the victorious proletariat against the bourgeoisie of other
countries) [8, pp. 751-752]. And from a scientific point of view, it would be
completely incorrect and unrevolutionary to bypass or obscure the most
important and most difficult thing: the necessity of suppressing the resistance of
the bourgeoisie during the transition to socialism. And in wars of this kind, to
recognize "defense of the fatherland" means to consider these wars "just" and
corresponding to the interests of the proletariat, since a reverse invasion of the
bourgeoisie cannot be excluded in any war and, accordingly, resistance to such
an invasion must be organized.
[Establishing a new relation with new components in this new relation in place of
the relation {Entente (Great Britain, France, Russia) / Triple Alliance (Germany,
Austria-Hungary, Italy)} (since new forces that entered into a new confrontation
and war were awakened: {proletarian plus national revolution / bourgeois plus
national-chauvinistic war}) requires finding a new correlation of these new
components in the indicated relation, i.e. finding a new balance of the new forces

Thus, analyzing the predatory conflict through the prism of the previously
incorrectly composed relation {people (instigated by the bourgeoisie) of one
country / people (instigated by the bourgeoisie) of another country} and
showing the hypocrisy and duplicity of the slogans of such falsely understood
